title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve Tool to Cryptographically Verify AI Model Inference
summary:
The company has introduced a new open source library called FlashProve that uses zero-knowledge proofs to cryptographically verify that an AI response was generated by a specific set of model weights. By allowing this verification without exposing the actual weights, the system is designed to prevent cloud hosts or routers from secretly swapping a requested AI model for a cheaper or tampered version.

In benchmarks using the 400B parameter Llama 4 Maverick model, FlashProve proved 110 tokens per second on a single H100 GPU with proofs of roughly 19MB. Previous methods for the same model took 14.3 hours to prove 1,000 tokens and generated 93.6GB proofs. Anthropic noted that its AI assistant Claude helped develop the system and that the project's security guarantees were formally proven in the Lean programming language, though the company did not review the AI-generated technical paper in detail.

selectedTweets.text:
HOLY SHIT. Anthropic just unveiled FlashProve, a zero-knowledge system Claude helped build that can cryptographically prove an AI response came from the exact model weights claimed, WITHOUT revealing the weights. That means a router, cloud host or attacker can no longer quietly swap in a cheaper or tampered model without getting caught.

On Llama 4 Maverick 400B, one H100 proves 110 tokens/sec with ~19MB proofs, and anyone can verify them in seconds on a CPU. The ONLY earlier proof of this model took 14.3 HOURS for 1,000 tokens and produced a 93.6GB proof.

And this is wild: because Claude “often makes decisions that are hard to evaluate,” Anthropic formally proved FlashProve’s top-level security guarantees in Lean. Meanwhile, the technical paper itself was AI-generated, and Anthropic says it did NOT review it in detail.
